title: Visual input in prompts, and apps with vision capabilities
learningObjective: Interpret visual input in prompts with a deployed multimodal model, and build a lightweight application that includes vision capabilities.
foundation: A multimodal (vision-capable) model can look at an image you include in the prompt and answer questions about it: describe it, read text, spot problems, compare it with rules.
In an app, you send the image (as a URL or encoded data) together with your question, and ask for a structured answer your code can use.
engineer: Responses API: input=[{'role':'user','content':[{'type':'input_text','text':'...'},{'type':'input_image','image_url':'https://...'}]}]. For local files, encode as a base64 data URI (data:image/jpeg;base64,...); the service can't read paths on your machine.

Ask for structured output (JSON with fields such as damage_type and severity) and validate it. Use a detail level setting where available to trade cost for precision; large images consume more tokens.
When you need fixed, consistent outputs (OCR text with positions, tags, captions) use Azure Vision in Foundry Tools; for schema-based extraction from many images use Content Understanding.
App design: resize images before upload, handle content filter results, keep a human reviewer for high-impact decisions, and never send images users haven't consented to share.
Errors: unsupported or too-large images, private URLs the service can't reach (use data URIs or SAS URLs), non-vision deployments (the model ignores or rejects images).

example.title: Car damage pre-assessment
body: An insurer's app sends a customer's car photo with the prompt 'List damaged parts and rate severity as JSON'. The model returns {front_bumper: medium, headlight: high}.
A first attempt failed because the app sent a local file path; encoding the photo as a base64 data URI fixed it. Claims over a threshold go to a human adjuster.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with access to Microsoft Foundry (ai.azure.com)
permissions: Azure AI User on the Foundry project to use models and agents; Azure AI Project Manager or Owner to create projects and deployments
limits: Model availability differs by region and deployment type
Deployments have tokens-per-minute (TPM) rate limits and quota per subscription and region
portal: Deploy a vision-capable chat model and gpt-image-1 from the model catalog.
Chat playground: attach an image and ask about it.
configuration.cli:
# Create a Foundry resource and project (billable only when used)
az group create --name rg-ai901 --location eastus2
az cognitiveservices account create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --kind AIServices --sku S0 --location eastus2 --custom-domain contoso-ai --allow-project-management
az cognitiveservices account project create --name support --resource-group rg-ai901 --account-name contoso-ai
# Deploy a model (Global Standard, 50K TPM)
az cognitiveservices account deployment create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --deployment-name chat-model --model-name gpt-5-mini --model-version <version> --model-format OpenAI \
  --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 50
configuration.powershell:
New-AzResourceGroup -Name rg-ai901 -Location eastus2
New-AzCognitiveServicesAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-ai901 -Name contoso-ai -Type AIServices -SkuName S0 -Location eastus2 -CustomSubdomainName contoso-ai
# Projects and deployments: use the Foundry portal or Azure CLI
configuration.python:
# pip install "azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0" azure-identity
import os
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient

project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=os.environ["FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT"], credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
openai = project.get_openai_client()

import base64
# Describe an image (openai = project.get_openai_client())
with open("car.jpg", "rb") as f:
    data_uri = "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()
response = openai.responses.create(
    model="chat-model",  # a vision-capable deployment
    input=[{"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "input_text", "text": "List the damaged parts and rate severity low/medium/high as JSON."},
        {"type": "input_image", "image_url": data_uri},
    ]}],
)
print(response.output_text)

troubleshooting.symptom: Model says it can't see an image.
troubleshooting.cause: Deployment isn't vision-capable, or the image wasn't sent as input_image.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a vision-capable model and the correct content type.

troubleshooting.cause: URL is private or behind a firewall.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a base64 data URI or a SAS URL.

comparisons.difference: Model: flexible reasoning in natural language. Azure Vision: consistent prebuilt outputs with coordinates.

misconceptions.myth: Vision models can read files on your PC.
misconceptions.reality: Send the image data or a reachable URL.
Validate and add human review for important decisions.

architectureDecisions: Use structured output for vision answers.
Use prebuilt OCR for high-volume text reading.
